newsitem.title: CANADA: Arakis confirms Sudan oil discoveries.
newsitem.headline: Arakis confirms Sudan oil discoveries.

text.p: Arakis Energy Corp said on Monday that it confirmed three oil discoveries on its concession in Sudan with production capabilities ranging from 2,600 to 10,000 barrels a day.
The wells, which Arakis said confirmed previous discoveries, included the El Nar 72a, El Toor 50a-14-688 and Toma South 88c locations.

Arakis, which has a 25 percent interest in its Sudan project under a recently finalized agreement, said the El Nar well, with a total depth of 2,444 metres, tested oil in the Bentiu Unit I and Unit II formations.
Well logs indicated 50 metres of net pay over a 107 metre gross interval in the Bentiu Unit I, it said.

Arakis said a 10-metre zone near the base of the Bentiu I was tested and had an estimated productive capability of 2,600 barrels per day. It said the Bentiu Unit II also tested oil from 10 metres of net pay over a 17-metre gross interval.
The company's El Toor appraisal well tested the primary target, Bentiu Unit I, and also discovered an upper oil-bearing Aradeiba sand, it said.
Arakis said the Bentiu Unit I had a production capability of 4,500 BPD on a 10 percent drawdown.
It said the well confirmed the El Toor structure to be "of significant size" and a 3D seismic program was scheduled for this year to further confirm the areal extent.

Meanwhile, the Toma South structure discovered last year with the Toma South 21d discovery well, reported to have a potential flow capability of over 10,000 BPD, was confirmed by the Toma South 88C well, the company said.
The new well is located six km northwest of the original discovery, further delineating the Toma South structure, it said, adding that the gross pay zone was 73 metres with 45 metres of net oil pay.
A service rig was moving to the location to complete and test the well, Arakis said.
Arakis said it was currently drilling the Umm Sagura location -- dubbed the "pink Panther" -- east of its Unity field and was rigging up a new drilling rig at the El Mahafir prospect.
Another two drilling rigs were expected to arrive shortly, one of which is a deep rig capable of drilling to 5,000 metres, the company said.
